comment: Major omission/misclassification: DHIS2 is listed narrowly under HMIS and ‘DHIS2 Tracker’ separately under PHSP, as if they were two products supporting two boxes. DHIS2 is a Digital Public Good and a configurable public-sector information platform. Core capabilities include aggregate, event and registered Tracker models; organisational hierarchies; reusable metadata/WHO packages; indicators and analytics/GIS; data quality/approval; alerts, messaging and workflows; offline Android; role-based sharing; APIs, data exchange and apps; and a global–local HISP implementation ecosystem. Sources: https://dhis2.org/about-2/ and https://dhis2.org/health-data-toolkit/

public.text: Major omission/misclassification: DHIS2 is listed narrowly under HMIS and ‘DHIS2 Tracker’ separately under PHSP, as if they were two products supporting two boxes. DHIS2 is a Digital Public Good and a configurable public-sector information platform. Core capabilities include aggregate, event and registered Tracker models; organisational hierarchies; reusable metadata/WHO packages; indicators and analytics/GIS; data quality/approval; alerts, messaging and workflows; offline Android; role-based sharing; APIs, data exchange and apps; and a global–local HISP implementation ecosystem. Sources: https://dhis2.org/about-2/ and https://dhis2.org/health-data-toolkit/
public.suggestedRevision: Replace the two narrow listings with a platform-level DHIS2 entry. Map the single platform to the logical capabilities it can co-realise—HMIS/RHIS, PHSP/eIDSR, registries/cohort tracking, facility profiles, community information, campaigns, logistics-related reporting and cross-cutting analytics—while clarifying that capability, deployment and governance choices are country-specific. Add the HISP support/capacity model as part of the implementation evidence.
